items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I played with Zoot and Jimmy Rowles

ctx.x: Yeah, I played with Zoot and Jimmy Rowles and I can’t remember who played drums, we worked at The Haig, that place where Gerry used to work. And we were there for a couple months and it was real nice but it was at that time I really, as wonderful as it was with Zoot, I just didn’t want to play anymore, it was getting harder and harder to play and write and I knew I was having to become a full-time writer.

items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: Johnny Mandel can't conduct for shit, and he knows it. He can write like a mother, but he can't conduct.

ctx.x: But L.A. is a funny place. I don't know what it is. I like to live there. But the music, I don't like it. I like a lot of the conductors in Los Angeles. I think my favorite conductor in Los Angeles is Jack Elliott. I've played for under (you say you "play under," you know, when you play for a conductor) Earl Fagin, a very, very fine conductor. But I don't think he conducts any more. I think he had a couple of heart attacks. He is a very fine musician. Billy May. You have to learn everybody's downbeat, you know;…
